scenes.summary: Bob and the local Bobs witness a gorilloid raid, conclude the Deltans are being hunted toward extinction, and decide to intervene indirectly by supplying flint.
After observing Deltan mourning, Bob approves Marvin's plan to build reinforced defensive drones to protect the tribe from future attacks.
Archimedes finds the planted flint, hides most of it, and sparks a trading frenzy when an elder teaches him and the tribe renewed flint-working.
Archimedes experiments with flint tools, invents a workable hafted axe, and uses it to mass-produce better spears that raise his status in the tribe.
The tribe's food supply improves with better tools and weapons, and Archimedes gains prestige and social standing.

A renewed gorilloid attack is repelled by the better-armed Deltans, and a lucky thrown spear inspires Archimedes to invent a weighted spear design and negotiate a new social bargain around spear-point production.

threads_opened.text: The Deltans remain under ongoing predation pressure from gorilloids, raising the question of whether Bob's indirect aid and planned drone defenses will be enough to secure their survival.

events.text: Bob and the Delta Eridani Bobs conclude that the Deltans are being hunted toward extinction by gorilloid predators and commit to intervening to preserve the species.
Bob and Marvin accelerate Deltan technological development by seeding flint near Archimedes, leading to renewed knapping, improved tools, and better spears across the tribe.
The Deltans successfully repel a later gorilloid raid with improved spears, and Archimedes follows the victory by developing a more effective thrown spear design.

summary.one_line: Bob intervenes in Deltan development after discovering they are being hunted toward extinction, and Archimedes rapidly turns supplied flint into a tribal technological leap.
summary.paragraph: A gorilloid raid kills six Deltans and convinces Bob and the other local Bobs that the species is under existential predation pressure. After debating the ethics of interference, Bob decides they cannot let the Deltans die out, approves defensive drone production, and seeds flint near Archimedes to see whether the tribe can be nudged forward technologically. The experiment works spectacularly: Archimedes rediscovers flintworking with help from an elder, becomes a rising figure in the camp, invents a workable hafted axe, and helps spread better spears through the tribe. When the gorilloids attack again, the improved weapons let the Deltans kill several attackers and drive the rest off, and Archimedes immediately builds on that success by improving thrown-spears as well. Bob ends the chapter more emotionally entangled than ever, hopeful that Archimedes may help pull his people back from extinction.
events: Marvin alerts Bob to a gorilloid attack on the Deltans, and the Bobs watch six tribe members get killed and dragged off as prey.
The local Bobs compare observations and conclude that the Deltans have likely been hunted for a long time and may be nearing extinction.
Bob rejects noninterference, asks GUPPI for a population estimate, and decides the Deltans are too few to leave unaided.
Marvin identifies an old flint source, and Bob chooses to seed flint near Archimedes while also approving production of reinforced anti-gorilloid drones.
Archimedes finds the flint, hides most of it, and triggers a camp dispute that ends with an elder teaching him how to knap stone.
Archimedes turns the new knowledge into a hand axe and then into better spear production, which improves hunting and raises his status in the tribe.
A later gorilloid raid is repelled by the better-armed Deltans, including a dramatic lucky spear kill that becomes camp legend.
Inspired by the victory, Archimedes modifies a spear with a flint point to improve its balance and begins negotiating a new role for himself as a maker of spear points.
summary.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from horror and anxious moral urgency to protective investment and cautious hope as he watches Archimedes help his people adapt.

known_planets: Alpha Centauri B inner asteroid belt

open_threads.text: Bob now knows replicants can go insane during unstructured subjective time, raising the question of whether he can stay sane through training and standby.
Bob is denied access to genealogy records and remains cut off from any living descendants or family connections.
Bob learns that hostile factions inside FAITH could sabotage or terminate the replicant project.
Bob now knows several rival nations are racing to launch interstellar probes, with the Brazilian Empire suspected of sabotage and armed competition.
Bob learns the FAITH facility has a hidden tactical nuclear failsafe that could kill him and everyone nearby if someone decides he is too dangerous.
Minister Jacoby leaves after threatening Dr. Landers, raising the question of whether he will act against the replicant project.
The launch turns into a confused orbital battle with missiles, military ships, and multiple unknown attackers, leaving the identity of the factions involved unresolved.
After disabling his endocrine control system, Bob begins fully mourning his lost human life, raising the question of how this emotional release will affect him going forward.
Bob concludes that at least one more Brazilian Empire ship exists and that USE, Chinese, and possibly Australian probes may also be active somewhere in space.
Bob's first cohort of clones diverges in personality immediately, raising questions about how future Bob society and identity will evolve.
Milo has found two apparently habitable living worlds at Omicron Eridani, but it remains unresolved whether Earth life and humans are biologically compatible with them.
Milo departs for 82 Eridani, opening the question of what he will find there.
Bill and Garfield now have a working subspace communications system, raising the question of how quickly they can deploy it across multiple star systems.
Riker and Colonel Butterworth agree to try building colony ships in Sol, raising the question of whether the surviving humans can endure long enough to launch them and where they will go.
Bob has discovered intelligent fire-using natives on Delta Eridani 4, raising the question of whether and how he will make first contact.
One Brazilian vessel escapes the destruction of the Alpha Centauri construction yard, leaving its destination and future threat unresolved.
Calvin and Goku conclude Alpha Centauri should be reinforced with combat-class Bobs, raising the question of whether Bill will approve and send them.
Bob has identified an unusually inventive Deltan boy named Archimedes, raising the question of how far his intelligence and toolmaking will develop.
Bob begins activating additional clones at Delta Eridani to support observation and development work, opening the question of how large his local Bob contingent will become.
Riker reprioritizes transport-vessel construction for refugee movement, raising the question of how much this will delay colony-ship production.
Riker has convened a global survivor assembly, but it remains unresolved whether the enclaves can create workable governance and cooperate on evacuation and survival priorities.
Gudmund Valter reveals that Spitsbergen controls the Svalbard seed and genetic vaults, raising the question of how this leverage will affect evacuation priorities and colony planning.
The Deltans remain under ongoing predation pressure from gorilloids, raising the question of whether Bob's indirect aid and planned drone defenses will be enough to secure their survival.

recent_events.text: Riker expands the Sol operation with two new Bobs and confirms that only about fifteen million humans survive on devastated Earth.
Bill receives Milo's startling report that 82 Eridani has two habitable planets and starts pushing the news toward Sol.
Riker brings Earth's survivor enclaves into a shaky new political process and discovers that Spitsbergen holds the seed stock humanity may need to rebuild elsewhere.
Homer decides to bypass Riker and pitch Butterworth a compromise on Spitsbergen's evacuation demands.
Bob intervenes in Deltan development after discovering they are being hunted toward extinction, and Archimedes rapidly turns supplied flint into a tribal technological leap.
